messages:
Alex R.: @here investigating a customer P99 spike for the continuous-batcher path — they reported tail latency jumping around 2:30 UTC. p95 up ~2x, p99 ~3x. Logs show a lot of tiny requests hanging in the coalesce queue.
Priya S.: Can you paste the quick metrics? p95/p99 numbers and the time window?
Alex R.: Sure — traffic window 02:28–02:36 UTC. Baseline p95 ~120ms, p99 ~320ms. During spike p95 ~260ms, p99 ~980ms. Throughput steady.
support-bot: Alert: customer-acme > p99 latency 980ms (continuous-batcher) — triggered escalation.
Marcus L.: Looks like typical batch-size vs timeout tradeoff: many tiny payloads forcing linger until timeout. Any config changes recently?
Alex R.: No rollout on batcher config in the last 24h. But I see a lot of short prompts (~30 tokens) and a burst pattern: many single-turn calls from same tenant.
Jenna M.: Do we have the batcher debug dump for that time? dump shows per-request arrival timestamps and batch closure reasons.
Alex R.: Pasted snippet from batcher debug log: 
```
[02:29:11.004] req id=aa1 arrive size=1 close=timeout wait_ms=50
[02:29:11.011] req id=aa2 arrive size=1 close=timeout wait_ms=48
[02:29:11.058] batch closed reason=timeout count=8 max_wait=100
[02:29:11.059] gpu_exec batch_size=8 latency=420ms
[02:29:11.480] req id=zz9 arrive size=1 close=size wait_ms=3
```
Marcus L.: Hm batch_size=8 might be fine, but look at many requests stuck waiting ~100ms for timeout — that pushes p99 up because a few requests hit the edge of the timeout then incur GPU exec.
Carlos V.: Could be request jitter + low occupancy. If some batches fill from burst and others just miss, tail gets hurt.
Priya S.: Repro steps please — we need a small harness to mimic the tiny single-request traffic. Alex, can you share a curl/script to repro?
Alex R.: Repro script (single-threaded, 200 qps burst for 30s):
```
for i in {1..6000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
    -d '{"prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":20}' &
  sleep 0.005
done
wait
```
Jenna M.: Running this against staging with batcher trace enabled should reproduce the linger timeout pattern. I can spin it up now.
infra-bot: Canary rollout note: batcher.grace_window default=100ms, currently set in-host to 100ms for prod.
Marcus L.: Quick mitigation options: 1) reduce grace_window to 30–50ms for tenant (canary) 2) enable tiny-request fast-path that bypasses continuous coalesce and goes to immediate single-request batch on GPU 3) temporary per-tenant throttle/aggregation at proxy.
Priya S.: Pros/cons? Reducing grace_window lowers p99 but increases GPU exec overhead (more smaller batches). Fast-path avoids wait but may increase token-cost. Throttle reduces external QPS but could violate SLA.
Carlos V.: For customer-acme, they prefer latency over cost. I'd try per-tenant grace_window override first (canary) then enable fast-path for that tenant if needed.
Alex R.: Action plan: (1) Jenna to canary-override grace_window -> 40ms for acme on 1 host at 03:05 UTC; (2) Marcus to prepare fast-path feature flag + rollout (if canary not sufficient); (3) Priya to monitor p95/p99 and cost delta.
Jenna M.: I'll apply the override now to a single canary host and run the repro script in staging.
Alex R.: After canary applied: staging run shows p95 down from 260ms -> 130ms, p99 down from 980ms -> 360ms on canary host. Good signal.
Priya S.: What's the cost delta? small increase in GPU slices due to more batches but within tolerance for acme's contract.
Marcus L.: Fast-path still worth prepping as backup — I opened PR #1428 with a toggleable flag.
Carlos V.: Also recommend a short-term routing policy change: for small payloads (<64 tokens) route to a node pool with smaller-grace preset to reduce cluster-wide noise.
Alex R.: I'm going to notify support to update customer with our mitigation and ETA for remaining rollout.
support-bot: Ticket #ACME-578 updated: investigating latency spike, canary fix applied, monitoring.
Priya S.: Follow-ups: (a) roll the grace_window override to all instances in the region if metrics hold; (b) monitor token-cost; (c) schedule postmortem to discuss default policy and whether to enable small-payload fast-path by default.
Alex R.: Thanks team — keeping thread open for rollback signal. If p99 regresses anywhere, tag me. :thumbsup:"
